notes.title: Update Details (22nd May 2017) - .44 Revolver - Big Performance Optimizations
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/53dce3d9c33f1991c24f11b39c28133e434e60b0.png[/img]
[h1].44 Revolver[/h1]
It's been a long time since a new firearm was added to the game, so I wanted to spend some time implementing one of my favorites.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/ce1d8251162b598887fbda41df28123fcedbdcda.png[/img]
The .44 Revolver packs some serious firepower, and is ideal for close to mid-range combat. The .44 rounds are a little more expensive than the 7.62's and the weapon itself requires weapon parts to craft. So players will need to open locked crates, kill some hunters, or raid a base before they can acquire the weapon.

I'm hoping the addition of the Revolver will add more depth and variance to the combat, and give players more choice in how they want to arm-up. 

Hunters don't currently use the .44, but that will come soon. I want to get some feedback on the firepower before I add it into their load-outs. The Revolver can be upgraded in the WorkBench like the other firearms. 

[h1]Big Performance Optimizations[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/02ca9ec99ab4d0ff0d513b9011fbe8455dd465a7.png[/img]
Many players are still experiencing low fps (even some with beefy GPU’s). Solid fps is a huge priority for me, as I know how negatively a low fps can impact gameplay. It’s an ongoing mission for me to get the game running as best as it can, even for low-end machines.

Running profiling tests on system resources during gameplay, I discovered a large amount of CPU used by the AI and their thought processes. I’ve done a full overhaul on the system and have trimmed a huge amount of unnecessary calculations being made every game tick. There shouldn’t be any noticeable difference in their behavior from a player’s perspective.

The impact of these changes (on my dev machine) is more than [b]+20% increase to fps[/b]. This could be much higher for players currently bottle-necked by an older CPU (or on laptops). I would encourage players to max-out their settings and see how the game runs on the new update.

[h1]Fiber visibility (hotfixed last week) [/h1][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/44cd900d5f7ef3a45d77ad00acacd1b8c7c88e50.png[/img]
Since the color-grading updates, fibers became even more difficult to spot, leading to frustration for many players. I’ve updated them visually to be more apparent in the foliage, and slightly increased their size. I welcome feedback on this change. 

Thanks as always to everyone giving feedback and suggestions in the forums. I try to read all the threads. It helps immensely when players share their thoughts on the current state of the project. Please let me know if you experience any issues with the update. 

Have a great week!

notes.title: Update Details (May 8th 2017) - Animal/Hunter Interactions - Graphics Color Grading Overhaul - Big-Base Performance Optimizations, and more...
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/72e30a9c2eb065748955d875c8ec4b74d3abc861.png[/img]
[h1]Animal/Hunter Interactions:[/h1]
One of the most requested features since launch. It’s always been particularly jarring and immersion-breaking to see predators standing side-by-side with hunters in their base. Finally, animals and Hunters will now fight against each other (regardless of whether the player nearby). Hunters are now at increased risk in the world, creating a more level playing field for players.

This also means players will not always be at a disadvantage when an animal gets involved during a battle with the hunters. The balance can swing both ways, and hopefully this will lead to deeper combat strategies and unexpected scenarios.

This has been a tricky one to balance, and there will surely be further tweaks needed once players have spent some time with the update (so feedback is welcome). I believe this change goes a long way to making the world feel more alive and dynamic. Hearing distant gunshots in the night, from unknown battles taking place certainly should help add to immersion. 

[h1]Big-base performance optimizations:[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/a8b327fa4c2866e876ecf12e4011f8e9b7c7a7f0.png[/img]
Many players have built huge structures (which I love to see in the Steam screenshots). However these mammoth bases have led to some degraded performance, which sucks. 

I’ve made steps to address this by implementing LODs for all base structure pieces and tweaking the lighting as they transition through the LODs. I’m seeing improvements of around +15fps while inside and near these large bases. Thanks to GameEdged for letting me benchmark my tests on his build (featured in the pic above). You can checkout his channel [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/gameedged]here[/url].

[h1]Graphics Color-Grading Overhaul:[/h1]
The in-game world just became a lot more colorful! I’ve done a full overhaul on the color-grading of the in-game render. This has been bothering me for a long time. The color pallet has always felt washed out and flat, with an overuse of grey and muted tones. 

The new color-grading enhances the depth of shadows and boosts the vibrancy of the colors. I’m pretty happy with the result, but please let me know what you guys think. 
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/e3f4e2d21064f154b511aacd755545dc47e41104.png[/img]

[h1]Other notable changes:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed bug where item hover-tip would popup without mousing-over the item.
[*]Increased distance and added distance-lowpass-filtering to gunshot and animal attack sounds (allowing players to hear distant fights).  
[*]Added loot spawns to Workbenches in hunter bases.
[*]Increase dropped gear expiry timer to 10 minutes in Easy mode.
[*]Fixed exploit that allowed players to hide under foundations and axe animals to death.
[*]Mounted floodlights can now be placed on the ground outside the base.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/12b89fff2e2f5f94dd00dfc26ae93c62c766e408.png[/img]
[*]Fixed exploit that allowed players to spam the craft button in the BCU to craft multiple items without deducting the appropriate power/mass.
[*]Slightly increased the range of the glowstick.
[*]Increased the hunter’s turning speed (they needed a small stat boost now they’re up against predators). 
[*]Fixed bug that led to some player’s profiles to crash on load, after the wearable armor update.
[*]Prolonged the duration that hunter corpses will remain in the world. 
[*]Fixed annoying gaps between windowed walls.
[*]Reduced how much mass weapon-parts yield.
[/list]

I know there are lots of issues that need addressing, and missing features needed. notes.title: Update Details (May 8th 2017) - Animal/Hunter Interactions - Graphics Color Grading Overhaul - Big-Base Performance Optimizations, and more...
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/72e30a9c2eb065748955d875c8ec4b74d3abc861.png[/img]
[h1]Animal/Hunter Interactions:[/h1]
One of the most requested features since launch. It’s always been particularly jarring and immersion-breaking to see predators standing side-by-side with hunters in their base. Finally, animals and Hunters will now fight against each other (regardless of whether the player nearby). Hunters are now at increased risk in the world, creating a more level playing field for players.

This also means players will not always be at a disadvantage when an animal gets involved during a battle with the hunters. The balance can swing both ways, and hopefully this will lead to deeper combat strategies and unexpected scenarios.

This has been a tricky one to balance, and there will surely be further tweaks needed once players have spent some time with the update (so feedback is welcome). I believe this change goes a long way to making the world feel more alive and dynamic. Hearing distant gunshots in the night, from unknown battles taking place certainly should help add to immersion. 

[h1]Big-base performance optimizations:[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/a8b327fa4c2866e876ecf12e4011f8e9b7c7a7f0.png[/img]
Many players have built huge structures (which I love to see in the Steam screenshots). However these mammoth bases have led to some degraded performance, which sucks. 

I’ve made steps to address this by implementing LODs for all base structure pieces and tweaking the lighting as they transition through the LODs. I’m seeing improvements of around +15fps while inside and near these large bases. Thanks to GameEdged for letting me benchmark my tests on his build (featured in the pic above). You can checkout his channel [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/gameedged]here[/url].

[h1]Graphics Color-Grading Overhaul:[/h1]
The in-game world just became a lot more colorful! I’ve done a full overhaul on the color-grading of the in-game render. This has been bothering me for a long time. The color pallet has always felt washed out and flat, with an overuse of grey and muted tones. 

The new color-grading enhances the depth of shadows and boosts the vibrancy of the colors. I’m pretty happy with the result, but please let me know what you guys think. 
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/e3f4e2d21064f154b511aacd755545dc47e41104.png[/img]

[h1]Other notable changes:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed bug where item hover-tip would popup without mousing-over the item.
[*]Increased distance and added distance-lowpass-filtering to gunshot and animal attack sounds (allowing players to hear distant fights).  
[*]Added loot spawns to Workbenches in hunter bases.
[*]Increase dropped gear expiry timer to 10 minutes in Easy mode.
[*]Fixed exploit that allowed players to hide under foundations and axe animals to death.
[*]Mounted floodlights can now be placed on the ground outside the base.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/12b89fff2e2f5f94dd00dfc26ae93c62c766e408.png[/img]
[*]Fixed exploit that allowed players to spam the craft button in the BCU to craft multiple items without deducting the appropriate power/mass.
[*]Slightly increased the range of the glowstick.
[*]Increased the hunter’s turning speed (they needed a small stat boost now they’re up against predators). 
[*]Fixed bug that led to some player’s profiles to crash on load, after the wearable armor update.
[*]Prolonged the duration that hunter corpses will remain in the world. 
[*]Fixed annoying gaps between windowed walls.
[*]Reduced how much mass weapon-parts yield.
[/list]

I know there are lots of issues that need addressing, and missing features needed. The feedback on the forums has been a massive help in prioritizing the issues, as well as some great suggestions and discussion on the future of the project. Thanks so much for all the support, it really means a lot. 

As usual, please let me know of any issues or problems with the update. Have a great week!

notes.title: Update Details (April 23rd 2017) - Centralized Exterior Base Lights
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/4a91ada6ba99a653a6550af106b5300f7f9e291d.png[/img]

Since the hunters began attacking player bases, night-time raids have led to some frustrating and underwhelming battles, where players were unable to see the hunters during the attack, and had to hide in their base, unable to fight back.

[h1]Craftable Floodlights:[/h1]
Today’s update introduces craftable Floodlights to provide illumination for base exteriors. There are two types of floodlights; standard and mounted.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/5df7437b313e0ffe034c552bb2b7a6b689faa6e7.png[/img]
Mounted floodlights come mounted on a stand (useful for placing on decking), while standards can be attached directly to base walls. 

[h1]Centralized Switches:[/h1]
Players can also now craft Floodlight Switches. The switches can be placed anywhere in the base and provide a quick means to flip all base floodlights on and off. This can be particularly useful during surprise attacks.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/7769bbc6a3522745e172d6752de2ebace4af8960.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/1a02c49edb38a842d677d7e343ae68b5dcb10835.png[/img]

The new craftable items can be found in the BCU crafting menu (let me know if the recipe balance seems off). Floodlights use more power than standard base lights, so make sure you have ample power and storage for when you need to use them.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/7c3b3e3d632e69d7130c90f155a0448c8c8b5ff7.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/38c1247b13eb0b6c54a2326da4da7c7cc9288da9.png[/img]
As well as many other minor bug fixes, I’ve put some work into automating my release pipeline, making it much easier to roll-out releases. These changes will also prevent players having to agree to the Epic EULA after each patch (although this won’t take affect until the following patch). I’ve had to tweak the default control scheme again, so unfortunately some players may need to reset their controls after the update. There has been a lot of work behind the scenes this week, which doesn't reflect in the current update content, but is necessary to move the project forward. Please stay tuned for future updates and details.  

As always, thanks to everyone that’s been supporting the project and giving feedback on the current state of the game. I read the forums everyday, so if there are issues you’re experiencing, please do share so I can work to resolve them.

Cheers

notes.title: Update Details (April 12th 2017) - Wearable Armor - Evolving, Geared-up Hunters - Camera Movement Physics - and much more…
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/62b53ae2a119ef0e59cb4113330fecb62d869b09.png[/img]
[h1]Wearable Armor:[/h1]
Since the last few updates, there has been an increasing need for better protection during combat (especially from lucky hunter headshots). Players can now craft the Combat Vest and Combat Helmet, both found in the default crafting menu.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/07dfe74f6ffd8f927ed1e33bcbc4bd69b60741de.png[/img]
[b]Headshots:[/b] Without head protection, headshots do 4x damage. Wearing the helmet brings damage down to 1.5x. So it’s still worth going for headshots when in a fight.

[h1]Evolving, Geared-up Hunters:[/h1]
Hunters can now make use of the new wearable armor. A new system allows hunters to gear-up based on the threat they’re under. Repeatedly attacking a hunter squad will force them to start crafting better armor in defense. 
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/86230a7291a7e9fe199c527288f4091e2dcf4543.png[/img]
The hope is that players who enjoy waging war on the hunters, will be presented with a tougher fight over-time, whilst peaceful players will face less risk.

The hunters will slowly gear-up regardless of whether they’re being attacked. However to a lesser extent than those taking repeated attacks. The extent and speed at which the hunters will gear-up varies across easy/normal/hardcore modes.

[h1]Revamped Clothing Profile:[/h1]
With the addition of the new wearable clothing items, I’ve reworked the clothing profile to allow extra clothing slots. Clothing items can now be added in any order (rather than specific slots for certain clothing types). They can also be added/removed by shift-clicking in and out.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/da6eba2fd0c9cb3bf31efcec08a35de3817747fd.png[/img]

[h1]Camera Movement Physics:[/h1]
Prior to this update, the camera movement remained entirely static while moving around the geometry of the world, leading to movement physics feeling stiff. Now jumping, landing, crouching, etc, prompts appropriate camera movement, giving a more weighty feeling to character movement. This includes when taking damage. I may further tweak this based on player feedback.

[h1]Tweaks to Difficulty Modes:[/h1]
[b]Easy mode:[/b] Animals and hunters now tire quicker when chasing players, allowing for easier escape for players that enjoy a more casual experience.
[b]Hardcore:[/b] Hunter bases can now hold up to 4 hunters per base (previously a max of 3). This, along with the new geared-up hunters will present an increasing challenge for survivors who enjoy hardcore mode.

[h1]Other fixes/changes:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Pressing the currently selected toolbelt item will unequip the item.
[*]Added audio feedback for dragging and dropping items within inventories.
[*]Fixed bug where hunter squads would stop periodic attacks on player bases if killed en-route to an attack.
[*]Cloth can now be crafted using cotton.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/6f040ac1b01810c1c40a8dc346b648533823234d.png[/img]
[*]Updated the default config and mouse sensitivity to better align with standard control schemes. Unfortunately this may reset current controls (which you can change back in the in-game menu, sorry for the inconvenience).
[*]Hunter jackets can now be torn into cloth.
[*]Added contextual hints of how to butcher animals, for new players.
[*]Removed sound indicating when the last hunter in a squad has been killed.
[*]Fixed bug where items wouldn’t auto-stack onto the last slot in the refinery.
[*]Fixed crash when loading a save game, when base names contained certain special characters (sorry to those who encountered this bug).
[*]Many other small updates.
[/list]
As always, thanks to everyone who’s been submitting feedback and participating in discussions on the forum. It really helps to hear directly from those playing the game, and I try to ready all the discussion threads. Please let me know if you experience any issues with the update.

Cheers

notes.title: Update Details (28th March 2017) - Base Armor Upgrades - Bigger Hunter Bases - and much more...
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/342f9315fe27675ffdb3976b9a97684f31ad393f.png[/img]
[h1]Base Armor Upgrades[/h1]
Since the last update (when hunter squads began attacking player bases) players have reported a greater need for base protection. Today’s update introduces armor upgrades for nearly all base structures.

Upgrades can be made using the Hammer and require metal Alloy Sheets. Alloy Sheets can now be crafted at the workbench (while also found in locked crates and in hunter bases).
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/dea1e6d51b8573c39dda2dc0ddbc33d758c69d0c.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/ca7c6942c0dfefd2f18d98f1ac83222ad869c454.png[/img]
Armor-upgraded base structures have nearly 3x the hitpoints of wooden, and are cheaper to maintain. Please let me know if the cost and maintenance of the upgrades is off-balance. 

[h1]New hunter bases[/h1]
A new and larger hunter base has been introduced. Also hunter base sizes have been staggered, such that early-game hunters will build smaller bases, and later game-hunters build larger. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/b1e19dbb8cd331e397cff9031b927804528797cc.png[/img]

This is only the beginning of the progression I have planned for the hunters. I know that hunter/animal interactions are needed, and this is high on the list of upcoming features.

[h1]Other changes/fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed multi-BCU bug that caused base items to go missing when reloading saves (thanks to Zuleica for helping isolate this issue).
[*]Fixed bug with second upgrade on the solar panels.
[*]Added refinery to the smallest hunter base (so more loot when raiding).
[*]Hunters will now build solar panels on their bases.
[*]Reduced chances of night-time hunter base attacks.
[*]Fixed bug where crafted items wouldn’t stack in the workbench. 
[*]Fixed bug where Refinery lasers would stay active when all ore was processed.
[*]Fixed bug where rogue hunters were attacking player bases, unprovoked.
[*]Health-kits now require 1*cloth to craft (I welcome feedback on this). 
[*]Reduced noticeable texture-tiling of wood base walls. 
[*]Fixed bug where domesticated animals wouldn’t re-enter the Animal Housing.
[*]Added new footstep and landing sounds for many surface types.
[*]Added new impact sounds for tools hitting ground and metal surfaces.
[*]Added slightly warmer tones for daylight color-palette.
[*]Repairs to wooden structures now heal more hitpoints (75 rather than 50). Meaning less resources required to make base repairs.
[*]New sounds for player landing after falls/jumps.
[*]Fixed broken LOD of wood doorway (would show incorrect texture when viewed at range).
[*]Tightened-up aim in rifle.
[*]Reduced time to disassemble base items. 
[/list]

I really appreciate all the support and help from the community. Player feedback and critique is playing a huge part in shaping the game as the project continues to evolve. 

Please let me know if you experience any issues with the update, and I'll see you on the forums.

notes.title: Update Details (11th March 2017) - Hunter Base Attacks - New AI Combat and Navigation System - Hunter Revenge System - and much more...
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/c2a7ed45c0dd6ea0a52cea7bb331f9af9eb2a8c9.png[/img]

[h1]Hunter Base Attacks![/h1]
Players are no longer invulnerable to AI threat by hiding in their bases. Once neighboring Hunter squads have partially established their bases, they will begin launching periodic strikes on player bases, in an effort to push them off the land by force. 

The frequency and ferocity of these attacks will differ across easy/normal/hardcore modes. Base repairs and adequate defenses will become much more important to maintain base-security.

[h1]New AI combat mechanics:[/h1]
Hunters are now trained to use grenades (and their squad-mates will react when thrown). 

They can also now fire through windows, doorways, balconies, etc. Players will need to utilize cover as best as possible when in combat. They are also now better able to judge arrow-drop when using the bow at range. 

Their attack patterns have also been changed, so should present more of a challenge on an initial encounter (rather than walking in a straight line towards the player before shots are fired).

Players that have become used to building hunting outposts to engage Hunters should be prepared for a difficult fight if using the same tactic.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/2408ebf4ca580560fa1d3d171a8638f13008ce85.png[/img]

[h1]Hunter Revenge System:[/h1]
Players should think twice before engaging a hunter near their home base. Killing a hunter by their base will not be forgotten. Once regrouped, they will launch an assault on the killer’s home base the following day. 

Hunters will still attack regardless, but at a much lower frequency, so make sure you’re prepared if you antagonize them. This should offer trigger-happy players more opportunity for combat, while peaceful players longer periods of rest.

[h1]New AI Navigation System:[/h1]
I’ve implemented an entirely new navigation system for the AI (Hunters and animals). This was required to allow the Hunter to traverse the entire map to hunt down players. However the result of this change should impact all player-AI engagements.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/7fd07b844e63addb8251e64abcec685dd9ce8f48.png[/img]

[h1]Animal starting levels across difficulty modes:[/h1]
Up until now, animals would have the same starting levels across all difficulties (between 1->4). This led to level 4 bears mauling players trying to start-out in easy mode. This has been balanced out so that higher difficulty modes result in higher animal levels. This will mean that easy should be easier, while hardcore will be more punishing. 

[h1]Other notable changes:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Added audio feedback when killing animals and Hunters (as well as a specific sound to indicate when the last Hunter in a squad has been killed).
[*]Reduced bow damage against buildables (doors, etc).

notes.title: Update Details (11th March 2017) - Hunter Base Attacks - New AI Combat and Navigation System - Hunter Revenge System - and much more...
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/c2a7ed45c0dd6ea0a52cea7bb331f9af9eb2a8c9.png[/img]

[h1]Hunter Base Attacks![/h1]
Players are no longer invulnerable to AI threat by hiding in their bases. Once neighboring Hunter squads have partially established their bases, they will begin launching periodic strikes on player bases, in an effort to push them off the land by force. 

The frequency and ferocity of these attacks will differ across easy/normal/hardcore modes. Base repairs and adequate defenses will become much more important to maintain base-security.

[h1]New AI combat mechanics:[/h1]
Hunters are now trained to use grenades (and their squad-mates will react when thrown). 

They can also now fire through windows, doorways, balconies, etc. Players will need to utilize cover as best as possible when in combat. They are also now better able to judge arrow-drop when using the bow at range. 

Their attack patterns have also been changed, so should present more of a challenge on an initial encounter (rather than walking in a straight line towards the player before shots are fired).

Players that have become used to building hunting outposts to engage Hunters should be prepared for a difficult fight if using the same tactic.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/2408ebf4ca580560fa1d3d171a8638f13008ce85.png[/img]

[h1]Hunter Revenge System:[/h1]
Players should think twice before engaging a hunter near their home base. Killing a hunter by their base will not be forgotten. Once regrouped, they will launch an assault on the killer’s home base the following day. 

Hunters will still attack regardless, but at a much lower frequency, so make sure you’re prepared if you antagonize them. This should offer trigger-happy players more opportunity for combat, while peaceful players longer periods of rest.

[h1]New AI Navigation System:[/h1]
I’ve implemented an entirely new navigation system for the AI (Hunters and animals). This was required to allow the Hunter to traverse the entire map to hunt down players. However the result of this change should impact all player-AI engagements.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/7fd07b844e63addb8251e64abcec685dd9ce8f48.png[/img]

[h1]Animal starting levels across difficulty modes:[/h1]
Up until now, animals would have the same starting levels across all difficulties (between 1->4). This led to level 4 bears mauling players trying to start-out in easy mode. This has been balanced out so that higher difficulty modes result in higher animal levels. This will mean that easy should be easier, while hardcore will be more punishing.

notes.title: Update Details (19th Feb 2017) - Big Performance Optimizations - AI Behaviour Updates
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/ec0951d793bd19bd287ae0c14b059e04f131a08b.png[/img]

[h1]Performance Optimization Overhaul![/h1]
Many players have reported performance issues and low or inconsistent fps (even on decent rigs). This has been a continuous concern for me, as I know how important a stable fps is for immersion and enjoyable gameplay. 

I have done a full performance overhaul and am seeing significant increases to fps. I would encourage players to max their graphics settings and see how the game performs after this patch.

[h1]Hunters now trained to use the bow:[/h1]
Both standard and rogue hunters can now use the bow, and have a full set of weapon handling animations. Also a new system for weapon-changing based on circumstance. 

[h1]AI spacial awareness:[/h1]
It was immersion-breaking when animals or hunters would just stand there while bullets/arrows landed at their feet. All AI now respond accordingly to shots fired near them. The hope is this will make hunting small game with the bow more challenging (and satisfying), as missing the first shot now has consequence. Unfortunately animals still don't react to hunters, but that will come soon.

[h1]SP profile stats:[/h1]
The SP launch screen now displays the number of in-game days, and number of deaths for each profile. I plan to further these stats in future updates.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/d3ec56647947ff2b561dfd981fc7b56dfe2cf4a1.jpg[/img]

Another small notable change is that the bow no-longer requires cloth to craft (relieving the need for crates to arm yourself during hardcore mode). Also, fixed a notable glitch that allowed players to spawn free arrows for the bow.

As always, thanks for all the feedback on the current state of the game. It helps so much to read your thoughts and discussions as I continue to iterate on the game. Please let me know if you experience issues with the update. 

Have a great week!

notes.title: Update details (5th Feb 2017) - Hunting Bow
notes.content:
Hi guys,

[i]Firstly, sorry for the delay on this update. I was away travelling for one of my best friend’s stag.[/i]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/0e511aaff5963a86b880bda6f3ec677b5f9b26b1.png[/img]

[b]This week’s patch adds a new Hunting Bow to the player’s arsenal.[/b]

Many players rightly expressed a need for more primitive weapons in the game. The Hunting Bow is a step towards addressing this need (as well as offering some challenging handling mechanics). The bow can kill small animals with a single arrow, however has a slower rate of fire, and requires precision-aiming to land hits.

Arrows can be retrieved, however there’s a 20% chance of them breaking (and will break every time if fired into rock). Currently you can not retrieve arrows from corpses (however this will change soon).

It’s advised to take some practice shots against trees to get a feel for the range and drop of the arrows.

There will undoubtedly be balancing needed to fit this new weapon into the game’s item economy, so I welcome any/all feedback. I’ve taken a lot of care with it’s implementation and am happy with how it’s feeling, but am ready to make changes to its handling once you guys have given it a try. 

As always, please let me know if you have any issues with the patch. See you on the forums.

Cheers

[i]Ps. I have a short stint of travel this week for work, but as soon as I’m back, regular updates will resume as usual.[/i]

notes.title: Update details (20th Jan 2017) - Rogue Hunters
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/54ef1e650566114d994e66286bba5cc0eefec56f.jpg[/img]

Hi guys, tonight’s update sees the addition of Rogue Hunters. 

Rogue hunters are less predictable than the existing hunter squads. They regularly pick new camping spots, and aren’t concerned with building large bases, instead favoring simple camps under the stars. Equipped with lower tiered arsenals and less armor, they present less of a threat during combat. However they can take the player by surprise due to their variable camping spots around the map. 

They will begin to move into the world a few days after the existing hunter squads start building their bases. Players with established save games will have them begin moving in within a day.  

The number of rogue hunter camps is dictated by easy/normal/hardcore modes, as well as the number of hunters occupying each camp. They can be disabled/enabled as usual using the checkbox when launching a game. 

My hope is that they will introduce more interesting surprise encounters, as well as providing additional looting opportunities for players looking for a fight. They are currently fairly rare, so don’t expect to see them around every corner. I’ll wait for feedback from you guys before tweaking their frequency and behavior.

As always, this update is intended to be iterated upon, so I welcome any/all feedback. I know there are many other things that need immediate attention (such as animal/hunter interaction, lower-tiered weapons, map expansion, further base technology progression, etc). I really appreciate everyone’s patience as the early access moves forward. 

Please do let me know if you experience any issues with the update, and thanks so much for all the feedback and discussion, it really helps a lot. I’ll be on the forum.

Have a great weekend!

notes.title: Update details (10th Jan 2017)
notes.content:
Hi there, another quick update. Here's a list of the more notable changes in tonight’s patch:
[list]
[*]Added new fire-starter kit item. Many players rightly complained about the reliance on RNG for finding matches in crates (especially in hardcore mode). You can now craft an ignition source with purely natural items.
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/0fe2b142a11e54ccf962c8d8e51f8f9bc8af7efd.png[/img]
[*]Reduced amount of matches spawning in supply crates (and from starter kit).
[*]Added hud indicator for condition of buildables. So you no longer have to use a hammer to find the health of a buildable. When you are facing the buildable, it’s health will show top-center (useful for accessing damage when grenading into a hunter base).
[*]Loot can now be found in several of the devices in hunter bases (rather than only the storage chest).
[*]Now a chance of finding crafted solar panels in hunter bases when raiding.
[*]Hunters now perform routine repairs to damaged base items.
[*]Enabled hunters dropping kit on death in hardcore (previously disabled).
[*]Hunters now occasionally skim the ash from their campfires.
[*]Small animals can no longer be permanently kept in inventories or storage chests. They will eventually die unless placed inside an animal housing and fed/watered.[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/0150f155ab505ce5422d8587bb7ef93cd249efc9.png[/img][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/b6a57caa78a0a5a72e68be555f786220661eaaa3.png[/img]
[*]Fixed bug where hunter base lights would turn on/off when no hunters were present.
[*]Jumping while crouched will now make the player stand-up (small thing, but used to really bug me).
[*]Fixed a couple of areas on the map where players could get stuck in the geometry.
[/list]
More substantial changes will be coming soon. I’m keen to continue taking steps away from such heavy reliance on supply crates and fleshing out the core gameplay loop, as well as building out the hunters and their behaviour. 

Thanks to everyone that has been patient with the early access bugs and balancing issues. I really appreciate all the feedback and suggestions that players have been posting. I’ll be on the forums as usual!

Cheers

notes.title: Mid-week patch notes (5th Jan 2017)
notes.content:
Hi guys,

I wanted to release a small mid-week patch to address some of the balancing issues with the new modes (primarily the Hardcore mode).

Prior to this patch the animals in Hardcore were way overpowered (in terms of stamina) and once a player was under-chase, there was little chance of escape. There was also an over abundance of resources, meaning seasoned players were not given a sufficient challenge (other than avoiding the OP predators and death). This patch makes the following key changes:
[list]
[*]A new stamina system for predators (including hunters). Predators will no longer pursue with limitless stamina, and will need slow their pace for short periods once exhausted. However they can still compete well against the player, so if you’re malnourished or low on stamina, you will be forced to defend yourself. [b][i]**Change applies to all modes**[/i][/b]
[/list]
Changes exclusively for [b]Hardcore[/b] mode:
[list]
[*]Reduced the amount of loot containers, ore nodes and harvest-able vegetation spawns.
[*]Reduced the loot quantity within supply crates.
[/list]
I also increased the lifetime of human corpses in the world. It was a bit jarring having the hunter and player corpses despawn so quickly (no changes to timers on gear drops).

It was awesome to see so many players trying out the new modes. The feedback has been crucial in making necessary changes to start improving these modes. Thanks for all the support and discussion on the forums. Please let me know if you experience any issues with the update.

Cheers

notes.title: Patch notes - New game modes (2nd Jan 2017)
notes.content:
Hi there. Hope everyone had a great holiday. Here are the details for this week’s patch:

[h1][u]New Game Modes (easy/normal/HARDCORE):[/u][/h1]
Much of the feedback from players has been that they either want a greater challenge or a rest from the high-stakes to focus on building etc.

These new modes should now give players more choice to play closer to their own personal tastes. Here’s some key points on the two additional modes:

[h1][i]Easy mode:[/i][/h1]
[list]
[*]Reduced amount of predators.
[*]Option to reload previous save game on death (or continue and respawn).
[*]Reduced hunter bases and the amount of hunters in each base.
[/list]

[h1][i]HARDCORE mode:[/i][/h1]
[list]
[*]Only a single life (however additional spawns can be purchased at the bed at an increasing cost).
[*]Heightened animal senses and aggression.
[*]Reduced starting kit (only an axe, glowstick and pants).
[/list]

[h1][u]Player and animal spawns:[/u][/h1]
I’ve reworked the spawning system to address issues with close proximity to animals when spawning into the world (for both players and animals). I also addressed the bug whereby animals could spawn in player bases.

[h1][u]Singleplayer launch menu update:[/u][/h1]
Many players rightly complained about the issue of accidentally clicking on [i]‘Start a new solo game’[/i] on an existing profile. Now existing profiles don’t display this option, and instead offer the option to clear the profile before starting a fresh save.
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/c44faa578c17ab237a9dc1e47c56de76f9a78ea3.jpg[/img]

[h1][u]Clearing areas of predators:[/u][/h1]
Previously, the respawning of animals was extremely quick after killing them, and in fact would not persist in a save game (meaning loading a save game would respawn all animals). There is now a more lengthy cooldown on animal respawns (which persists after loading a save). This means if you clear the predators from around your base, you will have a period of peace. 

[h1][u]Other small fixes:[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed exploit that allowed players the kill bears with the axe by standing on a foundation and repeatedly interrupting their attack animation.
[*]Balanced animal spawns in certain areas.
[*]Fixed bug where player’s dropped kit would spawn on the roof or upper floor when killed in a base.
[*]Added hints regarding dropped-kit despawn time, animal leveling system and free starter M9.
[*]Many other small fixes.
[/list]

I’m really excited for how the game will evolve throughout 2017, I have a lot I hope to achieve. Thank you so much to everyone that’s been supporting the project, and those posting feedback and suggestions on the forum (i spend a lot of time reading the threads). It helps immensely to read thoughts and feedback from active players. Please let me know if you have any issues with the update. I’ll be on the forums.

Happy new year!

notes.title: Patch notes (11th December 2016) - Solar Panels
notes.content:
Hi guys. Today's update see's the introduction of craftable Solar Panels.

Since limiting the BCU's to allow only one that will auto-generate power/mass, many players have been asking for additional means of generating power. Especially now ammo casings require power to craft. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/a0dd0048bddf01ab4d8e516526df8173800e0353.jpg[/img]

The Solar Panels are not cheap, but provide a trickle of power that can exceed the limits of what the BCU is able to provide. They can also be upgraded to further increase their power production. They can be placed on any base structures, as well as the terrain surrounding the base (although they are fairly fragile, so be wary of bears tearing them down).

Obviously the time of day affects their ability to generate power, and throughout the night they will not generate any at all.

The balancing will almost definitely need tweaking, so please let me know your thoughts if you feel it is unfairly balanced as it currently is (or needs nerfing).

As always, thanks so much for all your feedback and discussion on the current state of the game, it really helps a lot. I do try to read all threads.

Cheers

notes.title: Patch notes (5th December 2016)
notes.content:
Hi guys, here are the details of tonight's update:

* Zinc has now been introduced as a new mineable resource and can be refined down into Zinc Fragments.
[url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/3999f918e9c80b130568a80bad3e349bfe84fb78.png][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/2fd75b83d703ac98f4beee3f087fe3131cf900cf.png[/img][/url][url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/de6d0a8f3fdefac33ca1781acdf323bdefe0696a.png][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/d41692fb52547c41b37e79d9afc88b168bd8a2f1.png[/img][/url]
* Ammo casings can now be crafted in the weapons bench using Zinc, Copper and Scrap (also a small amount of power and mass). This is another small step towards moving away from reliance on crates for ammo. Also, hopefully better equipping players to fend against later-game hunter squads. You’ll have to let me know if the balancing seems off.
[url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/2314e8dae8635ec17244b1dcb6fab36059403068.png][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/c90e9ee68a9803875d1feee54b21fa1a0ae8e190.png[/img][/url]
* Grenade bounce has been reduced to ⅓ of what it was. This is a temp measure until better raiding tools and mechanics are implemented.
* Hunter base loot has been slightly increased (to counter the reduction of firearm damage to doors).
* Falling damage height has been slightly increased.
* Fixed bug where weapon bench craft recipe previews wouldn’t update power and mass as it fluctuates.
* Increased frequency of hints to build a BCU for new players (I’ll add an option to disable these hints in a future update).

Please let me know if the balancing seems off on the new changes (i'll be on the forums as usual). I know that a lot of systems desperately need work, but with gradual iterations and your guys feedback, I hope the game will start to gain much greater depth, and ultimately… be more fun to play.

Cheers

notes.title: Patch notes (4th December 2016)
notes.content:
Hi there. Here are the patch notes for the update that just went out. This week it's primarily exploit and bug fixes:

* Fixed a game-breaking bug where hunters would stop spawning under certain circumstances. If your save has abandoned hunter bases, they will start repopulating within a day.
* Fixed exploit where multiple BCU's in a base would provide additional mass (they can still be used to extend your base build radius).
* Now only one player base at a time will auto-generate power and mass. This prevents the exploit where players could build an exterior base and farm lockpicks/water/etc.
* Fixed exploit where players could build in hunter bases by extending their build reach using the numpad keys.
* Reduced effectiveness of bullets/shells on base items (including doors).
* Fixed bug where recycling weapons was giving way too much mass (and not taking into account upgrades). Now weapons with upgrades will yield more mass than standard ones when recycled.
* Fixed annoying bug where butcher icon would should when looking at a dead rabbit/chicken.
* Fixed bug where refinery and mass fabricator state was not saving on save games (which was resulting in them always being turned off and reset when loading a game).
* Increased hunter turning speed.
* Fixed bug where config and graphics settings would reset after an update.
* Fixed a couple of rock formations where it was possible to get permanently stuck (if you find anymore, please let me know).

Thanks so much to everyone that has been posting in the forums and letting me know about the issues they've encountered. I read the forums regularly and it's been awesome having you guys helping out as the project continues to make progress. It is very much appreciated.

I'll keep everyone updated as new content is added. 

Cheers!

notes.title: Stability - Update notes (27th November 2016)
notes.content:
Hi guys. I've just pushed a patch that 'should' address many of the causes of game-crashes players have been experiencing (in particular when picking up items from the world).

Thank you so much for those who have been sending your logs to help me investigate. It has been a huge help, and I'm truly grateful for your support.

I've also included a few other small fixes:
* Fixed exploit whereby player could keep generators/woodburner/etc fully fueled at no cost by spamming fuel into the slot.
* Added pre-baked collision caching for many of the world items, preventing collision needing to be constantly cooked at run-time.
* Found and fixed small memory leak in the hud application.
* Bumped the berry-water max stack count to match that of water.

I'm still committed to improving stability, and this patch will not address ALL issues. So if/when you experience a crash, it would really help if you could send me your log file (details here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/418030/discussions/1/217691032436912045/).

As always, please let me know if you experience any other issues with the update. I'll be on the forums.

Cheers

[u]Edit:[/u] There was a small bug with the initial patch whereby the fridge hud would get stuck. You guys let me know immediatedly (thank you), and it's been patched. Sorry about that guys, I'll try to do better next time.

notes.title: Update details (23rd Nov 2016)
notes.content:
Hi there, a quick summary on some of the main items in todays update:

* Potassium ore can now be harvested and used to craft gunpowder.
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/f6a391ff42c1b2db3ecb928d005f820bf25c0a78.png[/img]
* Grenades and gunpower can now be crafted in the weapons bench. Grenades can be used for busting through doors into hunter bases (or for killing).
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/3d395e97fa84d6e758751f89a7b45d94f5597716.png[/img]
* Axes/pick-axes now do very little damage to buildables.
* Fixed bug that prevented weapon upgrades reaching level 4.
* Rotten meat now burns.
* Fixed bug where power/mass was sometimes not charged for item upgrades.
* Fixed bug where weapons bench was drawing a small amount of power while idle.
* Removed exploit where disassembling wood ceiling quarter was returning resources for full ceiling.
* Injured animals now die quicker if not added to animal housings.
* Hitpoints to foundations has been increased.
* Hitpoints to doors descreased.
* Hunter base loot increased, and dynamically updates based on the hunter presence (a heavy hunter presence working a base will yield more loot).

Some may wonder why I'm adding grenades instead of more primitive weapons (such as bows etc). I know the game desperately needs lower tier weapons, and these will certainly come in time. However I felt I needed to start adding items that will begin laying a foundation for hunters posing a threat to player bases. I hope it will also give greater satisfaction when breaking into a hunter base to steal their gear (rather than just simply axing through their door).

I've also made good progress at isloating the cause of the random crashes, and hope to have it resolved asap. This is largely thanks to the players that have been sending me their logs (see this thread if yopu want to report crashes: http://steamcommunity.com/app/418030/discussions/1/217691032436912045/). I really can't thank you guys enough for the support.

The immediate plans moving forward are to start building upon the hunter behaviour and create a more believable and balanced purpose to their pressence. I know there are many other issues that need attention and I'll be trying to address these as I work on new features. 

As always thanks for all the feedback, suggestions and support. Please let me know of any issues with the update (especially any obvious balancing issues). I'll be on the forums :)

Cheers

notes.title: Update details (13th November 2016)
notes.content:
Hi there! Just a quick announcement on the update that just went out. 

I've introduced the ability for multiple save-game profiles (3 in total). This allows players to start out fresh without deleting their previous save. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/1243763fc7928b1ce2634c2b34d9130c1cb41c17.jpg[/img]

I’m hoping this will appeal to players that want to experiment with different base designs (and build locations). Or those that want to revisit the early-game survival with the knowledge acquired from their previous/current play-through. Existing save files will be migrated into ‘Profile 1’.

I’ve also been making many small balancing tweaks based on feedback (and watching you guys play). The Wellhead and Refinery have had slight increases to their power demands. These tweaks aim to give greater emphasis to the base’s power grid. I have plans to add additional craft-able items to support power demands in upcoming updates.

Also added some starting tips, as the game lacks direction for new players who are starting out.

Game stability is still hugely important to me, and I’m focused on resolving crashing issues that players have been experiencing. Thank you so much to everyone that has been posting their crash logs. It has been helping immensely in tracking down issues. This will remain a high priority until the key issues are resolved. 

If you experience a game crash (especially while picking up items) I would greatly appreciate you sending me your Launch.log file to subsistence.bugs@gmail.com. Details on where the file is located are here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/418030/discussions/1/217691032436912045/

Please let me know of any issues with the update. I know there are other outstanding issues that need work, and I’ll be working through these as things move forward. 

Thank you for all the support and feedback! It really means a lot.

notes.title: Update details (11th Nov 2016)
notes.content:
It can be a real pain having to rely on loot-crates for a water source. Especially if you're trying to support plant beds and animal housings, as well as your nutritional needs.

Today's update includes the [b]Wellhead[/b]; a new craftable item that aims to provide a renewable water-source for players at their base.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/4a4318e0099302c9afe2523506e420d85e7ca8aa.jpg[/img]

The [b]Wellhead[/b] is a powered item that can be crafted at the BCU. Once placed in the perimeter of a base, players must first drill down into the ground until a natural spring is exposed to extract water from. Additional power is required to extract the water. 

Power efficiency and extraction speed can both be upgraded. I plan to add additional upgrades to tap into extra resources underground (such as oil). Currently the extracted water comes in water bottles. This is simply placeholder until more appropriate water vessels are added. Please let me know if the balancing is off, in terms of power requirements, etc.

Fixes for many other small bugs and exploits are also included in the update. Including:
* Fixed issue where players could despawn ore nodes by interacting with them.
* Restricted weapons being upgraded beyond the 4 tiers per upgrade type (sorry if you had a lvl 10 shotty). 

I'm still focused on addressing the crashing that players have been reporting (in particular when pickiung up logs). If you experience a crash while picking up logs/fibers/etc after the patch, I'd appreciate you emailing the log file to subsistence.bugs@gmail.com. The log file is located: 

...\steamapps\common\Subsistence\UDKGame\Logs\Launch.log 

My next focus will be on the Hunters. They are still a very new addition to the game, and much work is needed to add balance and depth to their presence in the world. I hope to make raiding their bases more fun and rewarding, and ultimately put player bases under threat.

Thanks to everyone that's been posting feedback and suggestions in the forum. I've been trying to read it all, and it's been a huge help in tracking down issues in the current build. There is still a long way to go, but I'm excited for the future of the project.

Cheers

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/4a4318e0099302c9afe2523506e420d85e7ca8aa.jpg[/img]

The [b]Wellhead[/b] is a powered item that can be crafted at the BCU. Once placed in the perimeter of a base, players must first drill down into the ground until a natural spring is exposed to extract water from. Additional power is required to extract the water. 

Power efficiency and extraction speed can both be upgraded. I plan to add additional upgrades to tap into extra resources underground (such as oil). Currently the extracted water comes in water bottles. This is simply placeholder until more appropriate water vessels are added. Please let me know if the balancing is off, in terms of power requirements, etc.

Fixes for many other small bugs and exploits are also included in the update. Including:
* Fixed issue where players could despawn ore nodes by interacting with them.
* Restricted weapons being upgraded beyond the 4 tiers per upgrade type (sorry if you had a lvl 10 shotty). 

I'm still focused on addressing the crashing that players have been reporting (in particular when pickiung up logs). If you experience a crash while picking up logs/fibers/etc after the patch, I'd appreciate you emailing the log file to subsistence.bugs@gmail.com. The log file is located: 

...\steamapps\common\Subsistence\UDKGame\Logs\Launch.log 

My next focus will be on the Hunters. They are still a very new addition to the game, and much work is needed to add balance and depth to their presence in the world. I hope to make raiding their bases more fun and rewarding, and ultimately put player bases under threat.

Thanks to everyone that's been posting feedback and suggestions in the forum. I've been trying to read it all, and it's been a huge help in tracking down issues in the current build. There is still a long way to go, but I'm excited for the future of the project.

Cheers

notes.title: New update just went out
notes.content:
Hi there! Just letting you know the details on the new update that just went out:

[h1]Hunter balancing[/h1]
Players that have been playing for a long time may have noticed the hunter presence gets a bit out of hand, with multiple enemy bases sprouting up across the world. The new system adds a more manageable roll-out to the hunter's presence, as well a limiting how many hunter bases can exist globally on the map.

For those with save games where they are swamped in hunter bases, the new update will removed all but three of those bases. However those three will remain as powerful as they were before the patch. Starting a new game will allow the new balancing for their rise in power.

[h1]Stuck in the fence! (Map expansion)[/h1]
There were some awkward collision issues in certain areas around the edge of the map where players could get caught up in the fence. The issue (at least in the main problem area) should be resolved. Part of the fix for this required a fairly large expansion to the eastern side of the map. The new region includes some fairly distinctive rock formations that should aid players while navigation the map.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/f0ba639572d052a26445eabd946868f9787c5394.jpg[/img]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26620178/f1a10ffcf89a89e8696ec452965414e5b3e3d132.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hopefully resolved issue of game not starting for some players[/h1]
I was missing the C++ common redistibutables for the build in the Steamwork settings. If players still experience the issue of the game not starting, please let me know.

There are still many issues to resolve (including crashing, hud glitches, performance, etc), and I will certainly get to these ASAP. I also have much planned for the hunters as things move forward.

Thanks to everyone for playing. So many of you have been awesome with helping flag issues on the forums. It's going to take time to iron out the issues and create a balanced and fair experience for the player, but we will get there!

Cheers

ps. Please let me know if you experience any issues with the update.

notes.title: EA launch weekend update
notes.content:
Hi there! Firstly just want to thank everyone that's been playing the game since the launch. It's be awesome to checkout all your different base designs and to read your feedback and suggestions on the forum. It means a lot to know there are those out there that see potential in the project.

There's a lot of work to do, so thought I'd let you know some of the immediate things I'm currently working on, based on the continued feedback you guys have been giving:

[h1]Crashes when picking up items[/h1]
Many reports of this. I know it really sucks! I'll be conducting tests and trying to get to the bottom of this one. It may be a little while until I can eliminate it, so I really appreciate your patience.

[h1]Suppressed by hunters[/h1]
Players that have progressed very far, may have noticed the hunter presence is getting a bit much. I'll be making some changes for the next patch that has a more balanced roll-out to their progression, and how many hunter squads move into the world. If you are on a save where they have expanded across the map, unfortunately this won't remove those squads, although will dial down their ability to build up so quickly. Starting a new game will use the new tweaked hunter spawning system.

[h1]Caught in the fence![/h1]
Some players may have experienced getting trapped in areas of the fence. This can occur when the fence snakes around the geometry of the map (few problem areas). The fence pieces use a much larger collision plane then the actual mesh. This is used for a system that assesses camping spots for hunter squads. I'm getting this fixed right now and requires that I make an expansion on one side of the map (which happens fairly regularly).

I hope to get the new patch out this weekend. I know there are many more issues that need resolving (including a sweep to increase fps and some hud glitches), and I'll be getting to all of these in time. There's also several new systems in the works to add greater depth to the hunters and what they get up to.

I really do appreciate everyone that's been playing through the early access bugs and reporting on what needs fixing. This valuable feedback is exactly why I opened the EA and i'm truely greatful. I'll try to keep everyone updated as things move forward.

Cheers,
ColdGames

notes.title: Response to initial feedback
notes.content:
Thanks to everyone that have been playing the game and posting their thoughts (both positive and negative). Thought I'd make a quick post to detail a few changes I plan to make soon:

[h1]Hunter AI overpowered:[/h1] 
I agree that they are way overpowered for the current balance of the game. I plan to make it so that they have limited ammo (just like the player), and are forced to flee when depleted. I also plan to dial their numbers back and have them setup camp further from the player's base.

[h1]No meat on Lvl 0 small animals[/h1]
It is jarring that you kill a rabbit or a chicken and initially get no meat from it. While you do get high-grade meat from them by leveling them up in an Animal Housing, they should still provide some sustenance when just killed in the wild. 

[h1]Getting killed and losing your kit:[/h1]
Probably the number one topic in the discussions. I want to preserve a penalty to death (so there is tension while exploring), but I agree it's currently too much to lose everything so quickly (especially upgraded weapons). So I'll be making some tweaks to this.

I know this is only the tip of the iceberg of changes required to make the game more enjoyable. However this feedback is exactly why I opened up the EA to the public. I really appreciate everyone playing through the balancing issues and I hope you can stay with the project as things progress.

Thanks

notes.title: Update - AI Hunters (3rd October 2016 - archived announcement from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
[h1]Hunters:[/h1]
Over the last several weeks, much work has been spent on a new system that introduces AI controlled hunters into the world.

Once player-built bases begin to rise in technology, squads of hunters will now move into the world and setup camp. 

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_2bf1c305d840a1cbd2df30c43134e2cd40c6ded5.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_2bf1c305d840a1cbd2df30c43134e2cd40c6ded5.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

The hunters will build up their own bases over time, presenting a rising threat to players trying to establish a base in the area. They are fiercely territorial and will attack any players that encroach on their territory. Their behavior will continue to evolve over the next few patches.

[h1]Multiplayer:[/h1]
My hope is that this system will translate across both single-player and multiplayer. Hunter squads currently target specific bases based on how advanced their base technology is. This should should give some protection to new-spawns trying to get setup in the world. It should also provide greater gameplay depth for single-player and coop.

[h1]Release:[/h1]
Recent updates have also included many bug fixes, optimizations and new items. Gameplay balancing is constantly being tweaked based on feedback from the current alpha testers (and those watching the game). I really appreciate all the feedback (postive and negative).

I'm working really hard towards an early access release on Steam, so please follow the project if you'd like to test out the game once it goes public.

Thanks,
ColdGames

notes.title: Update (27th July 2016 - archived announcement from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
[h1]Animal Husbandry:[/h1]
Many new updates and features have been added to the game since the last announcement. Most notably, the introduction of small wild animals and the ability to catch and domesticate them.

[h1]How the system works:[/h1]
When small animals are shot-down by players, there's a chance they will become injured and stay alive for a period of time.

They can either be killed, or placed in an 'Animal Housing', where they will slowly heal and start to level up over time. The higher the level, the more resources they will yield when butchering the animal.

Animal Housing can be crafted in the Base Command Unit. Players are required to add food and water if animals are to survive in the housing. 

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_efbbbd3dfeeeba3113030e0a8ed989f8c7159058.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_efbbbd3dfeeeba3113030e0a8ed989f8c7159058.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

[h1]Fee-Range:[/h1]
The Animal Housing can be upgraded to allow free-ranging. When the free-range upgrade is installed, animals will venture out of the housing and graze nearby. They will return to the housing when players toggle the free-range option off.

Free-range animals are able to level-up to level 10. Without free-range, they will only reach level 3.

Short video showing the system:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ux8FfrltrQo

[h1]Summary:[/h1]
This update puts a much greater emphasis on the farming system, as successful harvests are required to sustain the demands of livestock.

Countless balancing, bug-fixes, graphical improvements, etc have also been added, but I think I'll focus on more high-level features for these announcements. Once the early access is released, i'll most likely provide links to the full change-list as the project moves forward.

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_c6929a9d21e5bc7126165816435044fe66583eb4.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_c6929a9d21e5bc7126165816435044fe66583eb4.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

notes.title: Update (15th June 2016 - archived announcement from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
A lot of big updates have gone in since my last announcement. To list some of the more notable:

* A new mining mechanic.
* A means of refining raw ores.
* Base item upgrade capability.
* Farming.
* Enhanced graphical updates and performance stability.
* Medicinal plants can now be harvested and used to craft health/adrenaline kits.
* Many new items, countless bug fixes and general improvements.

[h1]Mining and refining (overview):[/h1]
Various types of rock ore now spawn around the world. These nodes can be harvested using the new [b]Pickaxe[/b] to acquire raw materials.

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_54bc3b048b354534e98e6d567471446a703d23f0.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_54bc3b048b354534e98e6d567471446a703d23f0.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

The [b]Refinery[/b] can now be crafted from the [b]Base Command Unit[/b] and used to process the raw ore. This device draws power when in use, and can be upgraded to increase its number of synchronous processing slots.  It can also be upgraded to increase its power usage efficiency.

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_e18233e839484328275b8a4131ff655c1426481e.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_e18233e839484328275b8a4131ff655c1426481e.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_a47db57dc4978bf9c905aeb0bd5b4135efa7a04d.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_a47db57dc4978bf9c905aeb0bd5b4135efa7a04d.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

The refined ores are required for the higher level crafting and upgrade options, which greatly contributes to the pace of progression in the game.

Farming (overview):
[b]Plant Beds[/b] can also now be crafted from the [b]Base Command Unit[/b]. Seeds can be planted to grow various types of plants.

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_83a6f67443c37a74a0ebe7bda1500bb541310858.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_83a6f67443c37a74a0ebe7bda1500bb541310858.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_123eb2f6a919b51634be3e6f39129001da7e7fdf.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_123eb2f6a919b51634be3e6f39129001da7e7fdf.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

The [b]Plant Beds[/b] require water and fertilizer to grow plants effectively. They also require light. The intensity of natural light changes throughout the hours of day, and indoor environments provide less natural light. The various stats of a Plant Bed can be viewed when accessing it.

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_2711b643e2dfc929b43f10f22f43a5edf16c690c.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_2711b643e2dfc929b43f10f22f43a5edf16c690c.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/betagfx/apps/418030/ss_f5799127f63125c2c60efd4d1ab74f9504f779da.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844790&alt_url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/418030/ss_f5799127f63125c2c60efd4d1ab74f9504f779da.1920x1080.jpg?t=1476844791[/img]

Upgrades can be installed to add grow lights. [b]Grow lights[/b] draw power, however provide reliable light throughout all hours of the day and allow for plants to be grown indoors.

[h1]Release..?[/h1]

Lots of other new features and systems are in the works. Thanks again to those who have been helping test the game and giving feedback. Subsistence is now on the road to an early access release, so those who want to participate in it's continued development will be able to start playing soon.

notes.title: Update (26th March 2016 - archived announcement from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
It's been a while since I posted a progress update. Lots of new features and changes have occurred, and the game is getting much improved balancing and depth. Here are some notable changes since the last announcement:

* Several new updates to the animal behaviour, including new attack patterns and flanking tactics. Certain behaviour is only employed by higher level animals.
* 1st person sprinting animations for all weapons and tools, making movement feel much more fluid and weighty.
* Fat can now be harvested from animals, and used to render down into bio-fuel on the wood-burner.
* Meat now spoils over time unless refrigerated.
* Fridge can now be crafted to preserve perishable foods and runs on power.
* Players can now hold the sprint key and click on items to move them between inventories without dragging and dropping.
* Players now get half the resources back when disassembling base items.
* Generators now exclusively run on bio-fuel.
* Only members of a base can now access the Base Command Unit.
* Storage chest capacity greatly increased.
* Added many more 'snapping' options when base building.
* Adding too many items to fires/generators/fat-renderer now overflows back into the player inventory, so not to waste any items. 
* Overhauled the loot and animal spawning cool-down system. So now over-looting an area will force the player to venture out further while waiting for re-spawns.
* New variant of bear (black bears), that are smaller and less dangerous than the grizzlies.
* Added furniture items such as sofas and armchairs. Currently these are purely cosmetic, although will soon be tied into a 'comfort' system for bases. At this point they just allow players to add more personality to their building projects.
* Proteins bars can now be found in medical crates.
* Ability to reload previous autosaves has now been removed from singleplayer. Meaning the exploit of being able to reload after being killed is fixed. Now when you die, a save instantly occurs and there is no going back.
* 'Save and Exit Game' option in the singleplayer menu.
* Countless balancing tweaks based on lots of feedback from testers.
* Continued expansion of the world.

Many of the new features and changes are in direct response to feedback from youtubers and their subs, who have been doing detailed playthroughs and testing the game. I'm extremely grateful to those helping with testing and giving feedback, it's helping improve the game every day. 

I'll try to keep evenyone updated on the upcoming public early-access release.

notes.title: Update (1st Feb 2016 - archived announcement from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
A really quick progress update: Lots of updates have gone out since the last announcement. Below are some of the more notable features:

* Rare, high-value loot crates that require lock picks to open. Lock picks can be crafted in the Base Command Unit (at a cost).
* Greatly improved first-person hands model and skin shader.
* Mass Fabricators. Allows players to fabricate their own mass using power. Can be run in 'overdrive' mode which doubles mass production at the cost of power efficiency.
* Hammers can now be crafted, allowing players to repair damaged base items.
* Persistent character loadouts/locations when leaving and re-joining servers.
* Continued expansion of the world.
* Numerous balancing tweaks, bug/exploit fixes and general gameplay improvements.

Multiplayer testing has been running on a very small scale, and will be ramping up soon. Thanks so much to all those that have been helping test the game, it has helped immensely. Please stay posted for further updates.

notes.title: Update (4th Jan 2016 - archived announcement from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
Just a quick update on how things are progressing. Other than a week off visiting family and friends over xmas, Subsistence has seen many updates and improvements in the last few weeks. Here are a few notable updates (among many):

[list]
    [*]Improved npc AI. This includes improved path-finding and aggressive behavior towards players in their bases.
    [*]In-world vegetation spawns (berries, fibers, etc). These items are already integrated into the core in-game economy and crafting system.
    [*]Refined player movement physics, and tweaked many animations to improve gameplay fluidity.
[*]More base building pieces (including Wood Foundation Stairs, Compact Roof, etc).
[*]Skins for damaged base structures.
[*]Further expanded world.
[*]Countless bug fixes and general improvements.
[/list]

Much of the work (which isn’t mentioned above) has been prepping the game for the MP alpha, which I *hope* to start within a week. I’ll post another announcement when ready to bring in new alpha testers willing to participate in MP testing. 

Note: The current starting loadout is very much placeholder, and will change in time for the multiplayer. New spawns will not be armed with shotguns and rifles ;)

Happy new year!

notes.title: Update (7th Dec 2015 - archived announcement from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
Firstly, thanks to everyone who has been giving feedback on the alpha. Lots of tweaking and balancing has gone in as a result, alongside the continuous addition of new features. Progress is still moving very fast and I'm excited to start opening up the multiplayer servers in the next week or so. I have no idea what kind of bloodbath to expect, but it's going to be fun to watch ;)

I'm trying hard to respond to all the messages, but it's been a bit overwhelming the last few days since a few YouTubers have been posting play-throughs on the solo mode (so sorry if I haven't responded). Worth noting that none of them have yet managed to break through the early survival stage and move into the actual base-building side of the game (which is where most of the complex systems are).

[h1]For those waiting for testing keys:[/h1]
Keys are going out at a slow rate at the moment. I want to be able to fix bugs and balancing issues as they surface from the alpha testing before sending out too many. More will be going out soon, so please stay tuned.

[h1]Hint for players trying to get a base established:[/h1]
All of the advanced base construction options start from your Base Command Unit (BCU). This needs to be placed on a wall of your base.

[h1]Some clarity on the focus of the game design:[/h1]
It seems there is an assumption that Subsistence is primarily a single player game. This is simply not the case. Subsistence was built from the ground up to be a multiplayer game. The solo mode is there for people that want to go solo and build a base on their own, and still presents a challenge without the threat of other humans.

Ps. For those finding it difficult to navigate and gather at night; glow sticks are now a thing (see pics below), and all survivalist now come equipped with one.

Ps. For those finding it difficult to navigate and gather at night; glow sticks are now a thing (see pics below), and all survivalist now come equipped with one.

notes.title: Progress update and alpha testing (2nd Dec 2015, archived from Greenlight page)
notes.content:
[h1]Progress:[/h1]

Progress has been moving steadily, with lots of adjustments and additions based on the limited alpha testing feedback. Here are a handful of the many changes that have gone in over last couple of weeks.

* Several new base items (including wood burning stove, recycler, mass storage units).
* Additional building pieces. 
* Many additions to the in-game menu system.
* Damage skins for npcs.
* Continued map expansion.
* Hud overlays for friendly bases (allowing players to explore without losing their base).
* Lots of balancing for item spawns and base resource economy.
* Foundational work for multi-language support.
* Loads of misc bug fixes.

[h1]Alpha testing:[/h1]

Opening up the multiplayer alpha testing to a larger group is now imminent. The guys at PingPerfect have been in touch, and helping configure and setup dedicated servers for the early alpha testing. The group will start fairly small (and initially limited to North America). 

Some may only be interested in going solo, and just want to build a base by themselves in the world. Several keys will go out to these people also.

Thank you to all who have expressed interest in helping test the game. We’ll be picking from these people and sending out keys (with some info listing known bugs etc).

Will try to keep you guys updated.
Cheers

[img]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/394426147774073338/F119FCA9E2F5823C9937484A180F94710D3B904D/[/img]
